text:
lucy: Heads-up: Equatorial AI sent over an open-model license for EQ-7. It has a pretty broad 'no redistribution' line. Can legal/product weigh in on marketplace and SI implications?
diego: Paste the clause? quick skim will help.
lucy: Exact wording:
```
Prohibition on Redistribution: Licensee shall not redistribute, sublicense, mirror, or otherwise make the Model weights or binaries available to third-party marketplaces, system integrators, or resellers without express prior written consent from Equatorial AI.
```
lucy: They also note that "commercial use is permitted for API access only" in another paragraph.
rahul: That creates a problem for our Marketplace SKUs and for Dedicated images. If they block hosting, we can't provide images or cached weights to partners.
legal-bot: Running match vs Redwood Marketplace policy. Preliminary: incompatibility with hosting/packaging requirements. Flagging for manual review.
marta_pm: Marketing hold: please do not schedule co-launchs until license clarifications are complete. We need an explicit allowance for marketplace listing or a managed-proxy plan.
diego: Two negotiation paths: 1) carve-out permitting Redwood and approved SIs to host encrypted artifacts with audit logs and limited redistribution rights; or 2) accept API-only usage and we ship a gateway/proxy product — higher op costs and possible latency/billing complexity.
rahul: Tech notes for carve-out: require server-side encryption with CMK, short-lived signed download URLs (<=15m), per-object access logs, and a revocation API. Also require telemetry for usage-based revenue share.
lucy: Equatorial's concern is downstream repackaging. They might accept a carve-out if we include audit and anti-repackaging language.
legal-bot: Suggested amendment prepared: limited distribution license for "Authorized Markets and Channel Partners" with audit rights and export-control compliance clause. Want me to attach the draft?
lucy: Yes please attach and cc procurement. Also ask them to provide their export-control country list and whether they require client-side geoblocking.
diego: If they demand client-side only filtering, Hosted mode is non-compliant with our product expectations. Dedicated could still work with region-specific nodes if legally acceptable.
marta_pm: Also request a 72h PR embargo and approval on any quoted perf numbers in the agreement.
rahul: If they accept the carve-out, we'll add technical controls into our onboarding checklist: keys, signed URLs, replay protections, and automated policy enforcement.
lucy: I'll send the ask now: @equatorial-legal can you confirm whether the redistribution prohibition is intended to block marketplace SKUs and partner-hosted images, and if so, would you accept a limited carve-out for "Authorized Marketplace and SI Delivery" with the technical safeguards listed above? Please also share the export-control embargo list and preferred geofencing approach. ETA?
lucy: pinging product and legal to keep updated.
marta_pm: thanks all :thumbsup:
